battle.name: 古巴獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 古巴西部皮那爾里奧省查克拉科斯特
battle.brief: 一八九五年二月二十三日，馬塞奧與克羅姆貝特率三十餘人自西部海角登陸，掀開古巴獨立戰爭。西班牙殖民軍以七〇毫米線膛野戰砲為砲兵骨幹，沿公路據點用曲射砲火封鎖鄉間；起義軍則以散兵游擊與地方武裝在內陸周旋，雙方在皮那爾里奧省查克拉科斯特一帶拉鋸三年。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰的兩方是西班牙殖民政府與古巴起義軍。西班牙一方由馬德里的陸軍部掌握最高指揮權，駐古巴的「古巴軍團」歸總督兼總司令節制，一八九五年先後由恩里克・卡列哈、阿爾塞尼奧・利納雷斯、巴西利奧・奧古斯丁與卡米洛・加西亞・德・波拉維耶哈等將領接任。軍隊以本土徵召的常備步兵、砲兵與工兵為骨幹，輔以「志願兵團」——由本地募得、以古巴人為主而效忠西班牙的民兵——以及成立於一八五六年的民警「國民警衛隊」，民政則由總督兼民政長官與各省的省督分掌。海上由西班牙分艦隊封鎖古巴海岸，帕斯庫阿爾・塞爾韋拉自一八九五年起指揮這支分艦隊，他的運兵船隊把補充兵員與軍火送上哈瓦那、聖地牙哥與其他港口。起義軍方面，組織源於一八九五年元旦紐約「鄰里會議」與「蒙特雷俱樂部」定下的計畫，其政治綱領是一八九五年三月二日署名的《蒙特克里斯蒂宣言》，署名者為何塞・馬蒂、卡洛斯・曼努埃爾・德・塞斯佩德斯與胡安・帕斯特列；同年五月馬蒂陣亡後，反抗運動的領導層改組為三人「執政團」，由塞斯佩德斯出任總統。地面部隊稱「解放軍」，按戰區分編：西部戰區歸安東尼奧・馬塞奧，中部由胡安・帕斯特列與卡利斯托・加西亞分領，東部由弗洛爾・克羅姆貝特、赫蘇斯・梅嫩德斯與紀廉莫・蒙卡達各自成軍，營連多由莊園主組織的鄉村自保武裝與市鎮民兵改編而成，起義初期的人數雖少，編制卻是以全島同步起事為前提設計的。
countriesEn: The two sides in this war were the Spanish colonial government on one hand and the Cuban insurgent army on the other. On the Spanish side supreme direction rested with the War Ministry in Madrid, while the corps stationed in Cuba — the Army of Cuba — fell to the Captain General, who was at once governor and commander-in-chief; during 1895 the post passed in turn through Enrique Calleja, Arsenio Linares, Basilio Augustín and Camilo García de Polavieja. The field army was built on a skeleton of peninsular conscripts, artillery and engineers, supplemented by the Volunteer Corps, a locally recruited militia largely of Cuban birth but loyal to Spain, and by the Guardia Civil, the rural constabulary founded in 1856; civil administration was divided between the Captain General in his civil capacity and the captains general of the provinces. At sea the Spanish naval division blockaded the Cuban coast, and Pascual Cervera took command of it in 1895, his transports carrying replacements and munitions into Havana, Santiago de Cuba and the lesser ports. The insurgents were the product of a plan agreed in New York at the Meeting of the Neighbours of 1 January 1895 and at the Club de Monterrey, and their political platform was the Manifesto of Montecristi of 2 March 1895, signed by José Martí, Carlos Manuel de Céspedes and Juan Pastrie; after Martí was killed in May of that year the leadership was reorganised into a three-man Directory, with Céspedes as president. Their land forces called themselves the Ejército Libertador and were organised by theatre: the western zone under Antonio Maceo, the central zone divided between Juan Pastrie and Calixto García, and the eastern zone shared by Flor Crombet, Jesús Menéndez and Guillermo Moncada. Companies and battalions were recruited largely from the rural self-defence bands and town militias organised by the great landowners, and although their numbers were small at first, the organisation assumed a general rising across the whole island.
people: 西班牙方面最關鍵的對手是掌握武裝與外交的何塞・馬蒂・德・埃斯特拉薩。他以詩人、記者與革命外交家的身分在紐約主持海外宣傳、募兵、購械與航運，設立「古巴流亡基金」，把紐約、基韋斯特與各地流亡者編入起義軍，卻堅持由古巴人指揮古巴軍隊。他起草的一八九五年三月《蒙特克里斯蒂宣言》把起義目標從要求殖民治理改革提升為武裝獨立，規定一切權力來自被武裝起來的人民。一八九五年五月十九日，他在奧連特省聖多明各附近的 Dos Ríos 與西班牙前哨遭遇戰中陣亡，遺體無從辨認；後來古巴以他陣亡的這一天取代舊有的十月十日，定為國定革命日。安東尼奧・馬塞奧是戰場上最出色的起義軍將領，他以騎兵衝鋒與野外機動聞名，與克羅姆貝特等人完成西部登陸後在皮那爾里奧省連番作戰，多次以劣勢兵力在林莽與蔗田之間擊退西班牙縱隊，一八九五年七月進軍聖地牙哥，圍城受挫後損失慘重。克羅姆貝特是解放軍第一任總司令，長年行軍後病逝軍中。胡安・布魯諾・薩亞斯、卡利斯托・加西亞與紀廉莫・蒙卡達分掌東部、中部與西部戰區，赫蘇斯・梅嫩德斯則在聖地牙哥一線獨力支撐到一八九七年。西班牙方面主持鎮壓的將領輪流更替：卡列哈主張以快速縱隊掃蕩，利納雷斯接任後轉向韌性的消耗，巴西利奧・奧古斯丁與加西亞・德・波拉維耶哈把重兵集結在聖地牙哥與奧連特，真正扭轉戰局的是一八九六年底抵達的瓦萊里亞諾・魏勒，他推行「再集中令」把鄉村人口強制移入城鎮，企圖用行政手段切斷起義軍的補給與徵召。
peopleEn: The key adversary of Spain was José Martí de Estrada, who held the insurgent effort together on the weapons and diplomatic side. A poet, journalist and revolutionary diplomat, he ran the overseas propaganda, recruiting, purchasing and shipping effort from New York, set up the Cuban Emigration Fund, and enrolled émigrés from New York, Key West and elsewhere into the insurgent ranks, while insisting that Cubans should command Cuban forces. The Manifesto of Montecristi of March 1895, which he drafted, lifted the rising's aim from reform of colonial government to armed independence and declared that all power derives from an armed people. On 19 May 1895 he was killed in a clash with a Spanish outpost at Dos Ríos, near Santo Domingo in the Oriente province, and his body was never identified; Cuba later fixed that day in his place of the older 10 October as the national revolution day. Antonio Maceo was the most successful insurgent commander in the field, renowned for leading his cavalry in charge and for movement across broken country; after the western landing with Crombet he fought a running campaign through Pinar del Río, beating Spanish columns repeatedly despite inferior numbers, and in July 1895 he marched on Santiago de Cuba, where his siege was checked and his force suffered heavy losses. Crombet, the first General in Chief of the Liberating Army, died of illness in camp after years of marching. Juan Bruno Zayas, Calixto García and Guillermo Moncada commanded the eastern, central and western zones, and Jesús Menéndez held the Santiago line single-handed into 1897. On the Spanish side the commanders in charge of the repression turned over quickly: Calleja favoured fast columns and sweeps, Linares shifted to a war of attrition, Augustín and Polavieja concentrated the bulk of the troops around Santiago and the Oriente, and the man who actually turned the war was Valeriano Weyler, who arrived at the close of 1896 and imposed the reconcentration order, moving the rural population into the towns in the hope of cutting the insurgents off from supply and from recruitment.
kits: 本卡這件線膛野戰砲，是西班牙陸軍一八九〇年代野戰砲兵的主幹：七〇毫米一八八八年式野戰砲，銅質身管，膛線為阿基米德螺旋線圈，後膛仍靠人工從砲口裝填，藥包與彈丸分裝發射，是師、旅一級的伴隨砲。它的要點在膛線與藥室：用同樣的藥量，彈丸在膛線內旋轉得更緊密、更穩定，射程比前輩的滑膛砲拉長數倍，砲兵第一次可以在射程上壓過步兵。作戰時它通常由馬匹牽引的野戰車隨行，六至八人組成砲組，射程約四千米，最大射程可達五公里上下，配備霰彈與榴彈。西班牙在古巴另部署了更老的一批前膛裝填野戰砲，包括八厘米與九厘米一八七〇至八〇年代式樣的加農砲，同樣是線膛或半線膛身管；供城防與攻堅用的十二厘米、十六厘米臼砲與短身管加農砲則留在要點，後來在聖地牙哥攻防與馬尼拉戰役中才大放異彩。與此同時，軍方已開始引進後膛速射砲，前膛裝填砲與新式速射砲在同一支砲兵裡並存。起義軍的裝備極度匱乏：一八九五年登陸的數十人只有步槍、手槍、砍刀與少量從西班牙軍火庫繳獲的舊式前膛槍；攻佔聖斯皮里圖斯等城鎮時確實繳獲過少量七〇毫米野戰砲與山砲，但砲彈、馬匹與馴砲手同樣缺乏，砲兵在解放軍序列中長期只是裝飾性的存在。真正拉開差距的，是西班牙以馬車與騾隊運載、由前膛裝填野戰砲撐起來的「砲火—縱隊」體系。
kitsEn: This muzzle-loading field gun was the backbone of the Spanish army's field artillery in the 1890s: the 7 cm Obusier de Campaña Modelo 1888, a bronze tube with an Archimedean rifled bore, still loaded by hand through the muzzle, the charge and the projectile being carried separately, and serving as the accompanying piece of a brigade or division. The point of the design lay in the rifling and in the chamber: with the same charge, the projectile spun more tightly and more steadily in the rifled bore, and the range grew several times over that of the smoothbore pieces the gun replaced, so that artillery could for the first time outrange infantry. In the field it travelled on a horse-drawn field carriage, was served by a crew of six to eight, had a range of roughly four thousand metres and a maximum range of about five kilometres, and was supplied with shrapnel and common shell. Spain also deployed in Cuba an older stock of muzzle-loading field pieces, including 8 cm and 9 cm cannon of 1870s and 1880s patterns, likewise rifled or partly rifled, while the 12 cm and 16 cm mortars and short-barrelled cannon intended for fortification and siege were kept at fixed positions and only came into their own later, at Santiago de Cuba and at Manila. At the same time the army was beginning to introduce breech-loading quick-firing guns, so that muzzleloaders and the new quick-firers stood side by side in the same batteries. The insurgents were extremely short of equipment: the few dozen men who landed in 1895 had only rifles, pistols, machetes and a handful of old muzzle-loading muskets taken from Spanish depots; they did capture a small number of 7 cm field guns and mountain guns when they stormed places like Sancti Spíritus, but shells, draught animals and trained gunners were just as scarce, and artillery remained a decorative element in the Liberating Army's order of battle for a long time. What really separated the two sides was the Spanish system of gunpowder and columns, carried on carts and mule trains and built around muzzle-loading field artillery.
tactics: 古巴的叢林、漫長的雨季與幾乎沒有可通車道路的鄉間，使西班牙無法照搬歐洲式的密集方陣與連續射擊。西班牙的戰術形態是「縱隊掃蕩」與「據點防守」交替使用：以連續警戒線與輕騎巡邏護衛縱隊，護送給養、通訊與徵收稅款，砲兵配置在道路沿線的掩體陣地裡以曲射火力支援步兵，逐村清剿；同時沿公路每隔數公里設一座堡壘與電報線，企圖以補給線與交通線切斷游擊隊同鄉村的聯繫。起義軍採取的是完全相反的鄉村游擊：人數少、分隊行動、以莊園房屋、蔗田與叢林為掩體，主要攻擊西班牙的通訊線、郵驛、馬隊與後方補給點，盡量避免同縱隊正面交鋒，靠當地嚮導與農民提供的情報運作，一八九五年十二月二十日接近巴亞莫的「埃爾・霍比托」一役即以埋伏加奇襲重創西班牙縱隊。砲兵在兩個體系裡的位置截然不同：西班牙把七〇毫米野戰砲配在縱隊之前或兩翼，居高臨下用間接曲射打擊起義軍的集結地與村落，起義軍則找不到對等的火力，這也是一八九八年起義軍轉而以地雷與炸藥在城牆下攻城的原因——用爆炸代替火炮，用坑道對付砲火。
tacticsEn: Cuba's jungle, its long rainy season and the near absence of roads that could carry wheels made it impossible for Spain to reproduce the close-order formations and massed fire of European warfare. The Spanish pattern alternated between the sweep by column and the defence of a fixed point: columns were covered by continuous lines of advance guard and light cavalry patrols while they escorted supply, communications and tax collection; the artillery was posted in covered positions along the roads, firing in indirect curve to support the infantry village by village; and a blockhouse with a telegraph line was established every few kilometres along the routes, in the hope of severing the guerrillas' contact with the countryside by controlling supply and communications. The insurgents did the exact opposite: they fought a rural guerrilla war, in small columns, using plantation houses, cane fields and woods as cover, striking mainly at Spanish telegraph lines, mail convoys, mule trains and rear-area depots, and avoiding set-piece contact with the columns, relying on local guides and the intelligence furnished by the peasantry. The engagement at El Jobito, near Bayamo, on 20 December 1895 was an ambush-and-charge affair that wrecked a Spanish column. The two sides' artillery stood in an entirely different relation to this: Spain put the 7 cm piece in front of the column or on its flanks and fired indirect curve down onto the insurgents' concentrations and villages, while the insurgents never had equivalent firepower, which was why in 1898 they turned to mines and explosives against the city walls — substituting explosion for cannon, and sapping for gunpowder.
data: 起義軍的起點極小：一八九五年二月二十三日在西部海角登陸的馬塞奧一行僅三十餘人，其中相當一部分是軍官與有經驗的老兵；到一八九五年底，起義軍在西部、中部與東部三條戰線合計已有數千人至數萬人，確切人數各家說法相差甚遠，遠不能視為精確統計。西班牙方面，一八九五年秋抵達的古巴駐軍約三萬人上下，到一八九六年底增至約八萬人，一八九七年常被估計為八萬至十萬人，同期西班牙本土與摩洛哥的駐軍約在十萬人量級，兵源以本土徵召為主。火炮的數字同樣零碎：七〇毫米一八八八年式野戰砲射程約四千米、最大射程約五公里，砲組六至八人，野戰車自重逾一噸；西班牙在古巴的野戰砲總數沒有可靠統計，起義軍方面可用的野戰砲則只是個位數到十幾門的量級。傷亡與消耗方面，西班牙在古巴的戰役總傷亡常被估在數萬人量級，一般說法約三萬至四萬人，須同時包含作戰傷亡與死於熱病者；起義軍的損失同樣在數萬人量級，單是一八九五年在聖地牙哥圍城等戰鬥中就折損上千人。戰爭自一八九五年二月延續到一八九八年八月，前後三年零六個月。
dataEn: The insurgent army began very small: the party that landed at the western cape on 23 February 1895 under Maceo numbered only a few dozen men, a high proportion of them officers and experienced soldiers; by the end of 1895 the insurgents in the western, central and eastern theatres together numbered from several thousand to several tens of thousands, and the exact figures differ widely between sources and cannot be treated as exact statistics. On the Spanish side the Cuban garrison was around thirty thousand men when the reinforcements of autumn 1895 had arrived, rose to about eighty thousand by the end of 1896, and is commonly estimated at eighty to a hundred thousand during 1897, while Spain's own home and Moroccan garrisons stood at the hundred-thousand level, recruited chiefly from the peninsula. The gun figures are equally fragmentary: the 7 cm Obusier de Campaña Modelo 1888 had a range of roughly four thousand metres and a maximum of about five kilometres, was served by six to eight men, and its field carriage weighed a little over a ton; there is no reliable count of the field guns in Spanish service in Cuba, and the insurgents' usable field artillery amounted to a handful of pieces at most, in the range of single figures to a dozen or so. On losses, Spanish casualties in the Cuban campaign are commonly put in the tens of thousands, usually around thirty to forty thousand, and that figure has to cover battle casualties and deaths from tropical disease alike; insurgent losses were likewise in the tens of thousands, with more than a thousand men lost in the fighting around Santiago de Cuba in 1895 alone. The war ran from February 1895 to August 1898, three years and six months in all.
cause: 一八九五年的起事不是偶然爆發，而是十年間積累的結果。西班牙在古巴的殖民統治以財政榨取為核心：古巴是西班牙在美洲最重要的稅源之一，煙草、蔗糖與咖啡的出口被西班牙商人壟斷，農民的稅負與出口津貼制度互相牽連，一八八〇年代的「煙草戰爭」中政府提高煙草種植稅、限制本地製煙業，維希亞省的煙農因此破產。波多西哥西亞一八六八至一八七八年的「十年戰爭」雖以《桑洪條約》收場，換來的只是自治的願望與大批財產沒收；此後古巴要求自治、要求分享政治權力的運動屢遭拒絕。一八九四年西班牙在委內瑞拉邊境與美國交鋒時需要古巴協助防守，古巴起義者站在西班牙一方作戰，馬德里本打算以這次效忠作為給予自治的交換；但戰事結束後，在朝鮮戰敗、殖民地反亂四起、軍費枯竭三重壓力下，西班牙撤回了自治承諾，改派將領鎮壓。一八九五年新總督瓦萊里亞諾・魏勒到任後重啟對鄉村武裝頭目的清算、沒收財產與判處流放，數名準備在島內起事的地方法定代表被處決，數百名嫌疑者被流放或投入獄中，革命的火種由此被壓回地下。真正點燃火星的是紐約：一八九四年秋馬蒂回到紐約，與塞斯佩德斯、帕斯特列等流亡者商議島內同時起事、分路進攻而由海外接應，一八九五年元旦的「鄰里會議」定下計畫，三月的《蒙特克里斯蒂宣言》把目標正式提升為武裝獨立，於是西部分遣隊先行登陸開火。
causeEn: The rising of 1895 was no accident but the product of a decade of accumulation. Spanish colonial rule in Cuba rested on financial extraction: Cuba was one of the crown's most important sources of revenue in the Americas, the export of tobacco, sugar and coffee was monopolised by Spanish merchants, and the peasantry's tax burden was bound up with the export bounty system, so that the tobacco war of the 1880s, in which the government raised the tax on tobacco cultivation and restricted local cigar manufacture, ruined the tobacco growers of Vuelta Abajo. The Ten Years' War of 1868 to 1878 in Pinar del Río ended with the Peace of Zanjón, but what it bought was only the promise of autonomy and the confiscation of large amounts of property; the subsequent movement for autonomy and for a share in political power was refused again and again. In 1894, when Spain fought the United States along the Venezuelan border and needed Cuban help to hold the ground, the Cuban insurgents fought on the Spanish side, and Madrid meant to exchange that service for autonomy; but with the war over, and with the defeat in Korea, the colonial revolts and exhausted military finances pressing on all sides, Spain withdrew the promise and replaced it with repression. When the new captain general Valeriano Weyler took over in 1895 he revived the confiscation of property and the sentences of exile passed against the local leaders of the rural armed bands, executed several members of the provincial assembly who were preparing a rising, and exiled or imprisoned hundreds of suspects, driving the revolutionary movement back underground. What actually lit the fuse was New York: in the autumn of 1894 Martí returned to New York and with émigrés such as Céspedes and Pastrie planned simultaneous risings in different parts of the island, with foreign support; the Meeting of the Neighbours of 1 January 1895 settled the plan, the Manifesto of Montecristi of March formally raised the aim to armed independence, and the western column landed and opened fire first.
impact: 這場戰爭的影響首先落在西班牙自身：三年消耗戰耗盡軍費、抽空兵員，古巴戰場幾乎抽空了常備軍的骨幹，使西班牙在美洲的殖民防線全面空虛。一八九八年春，西班牙政府拒絕美國的干涉要求，又在美國指責西班牙在哈瓦那港炸沉美軍戰艦「緬因號」之後與美國開戰，新大陸的門戶在古巴島上被撕開，結果是西班牙先後失去古巴、菲律賓與波多黎各，美國接管了古巴的臨時統治。在古巴方面，三年戰爭把零散游擊隊鍛造成一支有編制、有後勤的解放軍；一八九五年五月馬蒂戰死被尊為國父，他陣亡的日期取代舊有的十月十日成為國定革命日，起義事業從此有了全國性的象徵。「再集中令」造成的飢荒與強制遷徙成為西班牙統治崩潰的決定性因素，也使古巴上下把美國視為唯一能終止戰爭的力量。一八九八年聖地牙哥與聖胡安山一線的圍城——以地雷炸藥破壞城牆、以線膛野戰砲與後膛速射砲在城郊互相射擊——成為十九世紀末常備軍與技術武器最後一次大規模對決的樣本之一，其經驗直接影響了此後歐洲各國的攻城與砲兵理論。
impactEn: The consequences of the war fell first on Spain itself: three years of attrition drained the treasury and hollowed out the army, the Cuban theatre took the very bones of the Spanish conscript forces and left the empire's American defensive line empty. In the spring of 1898 the Spanish government refused American demands for intervention, and after the United States charged Spain with the destruction of the American battleship Maine in Havana harbour the two powers went to war; the door of the New World was torn open in Cuba, and in the end Spain lost Cuba, the Philippines and Puerto Rico in turn while the United States assumed a provisional military government in Cuba. Inside Cuba, three years of war forged a scattered guerrilla movement into an army with real establishments and supply; the death of Martí in May 1895 made him the father of the country, and the date of his death replaced the older 10 October as the national revolution day, giving the insurgent cause a national symbol. The hunger and forced migration caused by the reconcentration order became the decisive factor in the collapse of Spanish rule, and it also turned Cuban opinion toward the United States as the only power capable of ending the war. The siege of Santiago de Cuba and the San Juan heights in 1898 — mines and explosives used to breach the walls, muzzle-loading field guns and breech-loading quick-firers trading fire in the approaches — stands as one of the last great confrontations between mass conscript armies and technical weapons in the late nineteenth century, and its lessons fed directly into the siege and artillery doctrine of the European powers after that date.
result: 一八九五年這一段的結局，雙方都沒有取得決定性勝利。西班牙守住了哈瓦那、聖地牙哥與主要港口以及島上的鐵路線，起義軍則贏得了廣大鄉村與民心：西班牙無法把軍隊長期深入鄉間，稅收與徵兵在起義區域近乎癱瘓。從一八九五年起，起義軍在西部、中部與東部三條戰線都建立了有效據點，兵力由年初的數十人膨脹至年底的數萬人，西班牙不得不把越來越多的正規部隊投入島上。技術與戰術上，線膛野戰砲在這一年並沒有扭轉戰局：西班牙以七〇毫米前膛裝填野戰砲維持對鄉村的砲火優勢，卻因為缺少能與起義軍在叢林周旋的步兵與騎兵，無法清除鄉村抵抗；起義軍則因缺乏砲兵與彈藥，始終無法攻下任何一座重要城池，七月對聖地牙哥的圍攻在守軍與海路增援下受挫，進攻部隊損失慘重而退回山區。戰局於是從一八九五年起陷入持久的消耗：一八九六年波拉維耶哈在西部推行再集中，一八九六年底魏勒接任後把再集中擴至全島，起義軍在韌性與補給之間取捨退守山區。直至一八九八年美國參戰，古巴的戰局才真正被外部力量改寫。
resultEn: In the 1895 phase of the war neither side won a decisive victory. Spain held Havana, Santiago de Cuba, the principal ports and the island's railway lines; the insurgents won the countryside and the loyalty of the rural population, for Spain could not keep its troops deep in the interior for long, and taxation and recruitment in the insurgent districts came close to paralysis. From 1895 the insurgents established effective bases on all three fronts, western, central and eastern, their strength growing from a few dozen men in February to tens of thousands by December, and Spain was forced to pour ever more regular troops onto the island. In technical and tactical terms the muzzle-loading field gun did not turn the war in that year: Spain kept the artillery advantage over the countryside with the 7 cm muzzle-loading piece, but for want of infantry and cavalry able to operate in jungle and broken country it could not clear the rural resistance, while the insurgents, short of artillery and ammunition, could not take a single important city, and the July siege of Santiago de Cuba was checked by the garrison and by reinforcement from the sea, the attackers losing heavily and withdrawing into the mountains. The war therefore settled into a long attrition from 1895: Polavieja introduced reconcentration in the western province in 1896, and when Weyler took over at the end of that year he extended it to the whole island, the insurgents buying their endurance at the cost of the countryside. It was not until the United States entered the war in 1898 that the course of the Cuban campaign was truly rewritten by an outside power.
